sentences.text: Chilenosuchus is known for its distinctive armour plating, which closely resembles that of the aetosaur Typothorax.
Fossils of this animal were discovered in the El Bordo Formation within the Antofagasta Region of northern Chile.
Researchers have proposed that Chilenosuchus belongs to the clade Typothoracisinae alongside Typothorax and other similar aetosaurs.
However, the exact position of Chilenosuchus within the family Stagonolepididae remains uncertain due to a lack of substantial material.
A 2003 reevaluation confirmed that Chilenosuchus lived during the Triassic period, specifically from the Carnian to the Rhaetian stages, approximately 237 to 201.4 million years ago.

There was initial controversy regarding the age of the strata containing Chilenosuchus fossils, as plant and invertebrate fossils suggested a Carboniferous or Early Permian age, which conflicts with the known appearance of aetosaurs in the Late Triassic.
